messages_body:
Hi Emma and team,

We observed an unusual saturation event in your dedicated GPU pool this morning (Jun 29). Some context: a spike in long-sequence inference jobs queued concurrently with a regional maintenance window caused the allocator to hit soft limits and trigger request throttling for ~42 minutes. Impact observed: elevated latency and a subset of jobs queued beyond your SLA SLOs.

Immediate actions taken by Redwood: 
- Rerouted burst traffic to compatible warm nodes in us-west-2 to reduce tail latency.
- Expanded batch window temporarily (safe vs. model quality) to increase throughput.
- Kicked an emergency rebalancer that moved low-priority workloads out of your pool.

We've attached a short runbook that documents the exact steps we executed and the logs we captured: [Attachment: saturation_runbook_v1.pdf (PDF, 1.2MB)], plus the allocator trace CSV: [Attachment: allocation_logs_0629.csv].

Proposed next steps for today: 
1) Quick sync (20 minutes) so we can walk through the runbook and agree on immediate guardrails (suggested: 16:00 PT).
2) Approve a targeted configuration change to increase your reserved burst capacity by 15% for the next 72 hours while we complete the root-cause analysis.
3) If you'd like, our finance team can prepare a provisional credit to offset observable SLA breaches — I can loop them in.

Sorry for the disruption — we're treating this as high priority and will provide a full timeline and RCA within 72 hours.

Best,
Jonas
Head of Customer Reliability
Redwood Inference

On Fri, Jun 29, 2028 at 14:58 Emma Li <emma@bluearc.ai> wrote:
> We saw a spike from our side and several inference jobs timed out. Please confirm impact and timeline.
Jonas — thanks for the quick update.

We had a number of production traffic spikes at 14:45 PT (models serving long conversations for chat assistants). This caused customer-visible errors for a few minutes; several teams at BlueArc flagged the issue as P1.

Quick Qs: 
- Can you confirm whether the reroute to warm nodes preserved model version parity (we can't accept degraded model variants without QA sign-off)?
- We need a clear statement on credits and whether this will be on our June invoice or applied as a one-off. Procurement looped in.

We can take a 20-minute call at 16:00 PT. Please include whoever owns billing/credits.

— Emma
VP Ops, BlueArc AI
Emma — apologies for the disruption and thanks for the details. I’m copying Marissa (CS) into the thread so she can coordinate post-incident comms and the credit calculation.

To answer your questions: 
- Reroute fidelity: the warm nodes were pinned to the same model version and identical quantization profile; no model variant change was applied. We validated sample outputs post-reroute and did not see coherent drift. We included sample KV checks in the runbook.

Root cause summary (preliminary): allocator backpressure + concurrent maintenance reduction in available warm capacity + an atypically high proportion of long-sequence requests that prevented effective batching.

Mitigation plan (short/medium term):
- Short (hours): increase reserved burst capacity for BlueArc by 15% (automated policy change we can revert).
- Medium (48–72 hrs): patch allocator to prefer preemptible low-priority jobs for eviction earlier in the cycle; release scheduled for 48 hours.
- Medium/Long (2–4 weeks): quota-based admission for extremely long sequences + synthetic warmups for your heavy job patterns.

Credits: attached is a draft credit calc based on your observed user impact and token-minute weighting: [Attachment: proposed_credit_calculation_0701.xlsx]. We propose a provisional credit equal to 40% of the impacted usage minutes this incident. Finance will finalize once BlueArc confirms scope.

Call notes: 16:00 PT works for us. Agenda: incident timeline, immediate guardrails, credit proposal, scheduled patch timeline, and confirmation of postmortem delivery date.

Best,
Ben Carter
Senior Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

On Jun 29, 2028 at 16:02 Emma Li <emma@bluearc.ai> wrote:
> Confirmed — Jonas and Ben, please include the CS contact for follow-up and procurement for credits.
Hi Emma and BlueArc procurement team,

Thanks for taking the call earlier — appreciated the timely sync. Per our conversation, this message summarizes the agreed playbook and asks for your sign-off so we can proceed: 

Agreed immediate actions (we've already applied these):
- +15% reserved burst capacity for the next 72 hours (auto-revert on Jul 4 08:00 PT).
- Emergency eviction policy adjusted to prioritize low-priority background jobs.
- Continuous telemetry dashboard shared (link below) for your SREs.

Deliverables and timeline:
- RCA draft (72 hours) — includes timeline, root cause analysis, and detailed mitigation plan.
- Permanent allocator patch (target: 48 hours) to change eviction order + admission control for long sequences (staged rollout).
- Final postmortem and customer-impact reconciliation (including final credit calculation) within 10 business days.

Credit proposal (summary):
- Provisional credit: 40% of impacted usage minutes (applied as an invoice credit against July charges unless you request a different approach).
- Final credit will be adjusted after we confirm scope of impacted jobs and any overlapping maintenance windows.

Action items for BlueArc: 
1) Reply to this thread with approval to: (A) keep the +15% burst reservation active for 72 hours; and (B) accept provisional credit approach (invoice credit by default).
2) Provide the procurement contact name for final invoice adjustments (we have procurement@bluearc.ai in CC — if you'd like a different contact please reply).

Links and artifacts: 
- Runbook: https://docs.redwood.com/runbooks/saturation_runbook_v1
- Allocator logs: https://s3.redwood.com/logs/allocs/bluearc/2028-06-29/allocation_logs_0629.csv
- HubSpot deal: https://hubspot.company/deal/7421

Thanks — once you confirm we'll schedule a short maintenance window for the allocator patch (non-disruptive; staged warmup).

Best regards,
Ben Carter
Senior Customer Reliability Engineer
Redwood Inference

[Attachment: proposed_credit_calculation_0701.xlsx (XLSX, 24KB)]
Ben — thank you and the team for the clear summary and for the quick remediation. BlueArc confirms: 
1) Approve +15% burst reservation for 72 hours.
2) Accept provisional invoice credit (apply to July invoice).
3) Procurements: procurement@bluearc.ai is the right contact.

We expect the RCA and final postmortem. Please include an itemized list of any jobs you consider out of scope for the credit calculation so our billing team can reconcile quickly. Also include a short FAQ we can share with our internal stakeholders about why the incident occurred and what to expect next.

Thanks again for the responsiveness.

— Emma
VP Ops, BlueArc AI
